Electricity Business Act Art. 38(1) proviso: electrical works on the same premises as a power-generating facility that is not a small-scale generating facility are excluded, and 'low voltage' is defined by ministerial ordinance. Enforcement Regulations Art. 48(1) sets 600 V. The explanation's statement that low voltage is 600 V or less is supported by the attached e-Gov text.

Choices (1) and (3): power is received at 6.6 kV, so it does not come through a low-voltage receiving line (600 V or less), and Art. 38(1)(i) is not met. The choice explanations correctly add that received power of 60 kW or 45 kW is not a separate statutory ceiling.

Choice (2): Enforcement Regulations Art. 48(2)(iv) treats internal-combustion generation only under 10 kW as a small-scale generating facility. At 15 kW this unit is not one, so the Art. 38(1) proviso excludes the whole premises. This reasoning checks out.

Choice (4): 7+15=22 kW is under 50 kW, so the Art. 48(2) proviso (combined output of 50 kW or more) does not apply, and both units are small-scale generating facilities (wind under 20 kW per Art. 48(2)(ii)). Art. 48(4)(ii) sets the general-use threshold for wind at 0 kW, so under Art. 38(1)(ii)(a) (output below the threshold) no wind unit can be general-use. The wind unit is a small-scale business-use electrical work under Art. 38(3)(i), so the installation as a whole is not general-use. This matches the explanation.

Choice (5): power is received at 200 V (600 V or less). The 5 kW solar unit is below the 10 kW threshold in Art. 48(4)(i), so Art. 38(1)(ii)(a) is met. It is also a small-scale generating facility under Art. 48(2)(i) (under 50 kW), so the proviso does not apply, and the premise of the question satisfies Art. 38(1)(ii)(b). It is therefore general-use, consistent with the official answer.

Choice (1): Electrical Work Act Art. 2(2) removes demand facilities of 500 kW or more from the covered private-use installations, so 250 kW is covered. Art. 3(1) lets a first-class electrician do this work. Appropriate.

Choice (2): a 3 kW solar unit is under the 10 kW threshold in Electricity Business Act Enforcement Regulations Art. 48(4)(i), so it is general-use. Electrical Work Act Art. 3(2) lets a second-class electrician work on general-use installations. The choice explanation's note that there is no separate qualification limit is also correct. Appropriate.

Choice (3): Electrical Work Act Enforcement Regulations Art. 2-2(1)(ii) makes work on emergency backup generators (engine, generator, switchboard, etc.) special electrical work. Art. 3(1) excludes 'work specified in paragraph 3' in parentheses, and Art. 3(3) requires a special electrical work qualification holder. A first-class electrician's licence alone is not enough, so this choice is inappropriate, matching the official answer. The choice explanation is correct.

Choice (4): neon work under Enforcement Regulations Art. 2-2(1)(i) is limited to private-use installations under Act Art. 3(3). Neon work on a general-use installation falls under Art. 3(2), so a second-class electrician may do it. Appropriate, and the choice explanation is correct.

Choice (5): 250 kW is a covered private-use installation. Enforcement Regulations Art. 2-3 defines simple electrical work as work on private-use installations used at 600 V or less, excluding lines. Grounding work on a 200 V motor falls in that range, and Act Art. 3(4) lets a certified electrical work engineer do it. Appropriate, and the choice explanation is correct.
